title.narrative: A locally and privately managed value chain to treat and value feacal sludges to improve living conditions and protect mangroves from littering in Diembering

description.narrative: This project, led by Gret, aims to strengthen a small private sanitation company named CTD de Kabrousse, which has been operating a combined solid waste/sludge collection and treatment plant in Diembering, southern Senegal since 2006.CTD is a women-led enterprise with significant potential to improve its business, both technically and operationally. Therefore, capacity building will be provided to strengthen the enterprise in financial management, HR management and marketing and communication aspects. In addition, technical support will focus on upgrading the old infrastructures to increase treatment capacity and in collaboration with the start-up Filtre Plante, they will construct 'planted drying beds', creating a low-tech nature-based solution for wastewater and sludge treatment. Finally, a local PPP model will be established to ensure institutional sustainability.The overall objective of the project is to improve living conditions and the environment in the municipality of Diembering (25,000 inhabitants) by improving the operations of the existing private sanitation operator. Moreover, CTD represents an interesting business model for waste and sludge management services for secondary towns in Senegal, hence the project will monitor and explore the potential for scaling up to other small secondary Senegalese towns.

title.narrative: S1- Total number of current unique users served by the initiative with access to improved and safe sanitation products and services

description.narrative: Fill in total number of unique current users for sanitation. Disaggregated per: Male/Female. Type: Domestic users (private and households), school users and for other public users (e.g markets and hospitals, communal users etc) Finally disaggregate users that are provided with a Safely managed / Basic service / Limited service from the initiative. The initiative must tick all criteria to be considered as that service level. 1) Safely managed service: - the initiative provides an improved sanitation facility (this includes: flush/pour flush to piped sewer system, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, composting toilets or pit latrines with slabs) - the initiative's sanitation service is not shared with other households - the initiative ensures that human excreta are safely disposed in situ or transported and treated off-site 2) Basic service: - the initiative provides an improved sanitation facility (this includes: flush/pour flush to piped sewer system, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, composting toilets or pit latrines with slabs) - the initiative's sanitation facility is not shared with other households - initiative does not ensure that human excreta and urine is safely disposed / transported / treated 3) Limited service: Usually at baseline level, but cannot be included at target level. This includes, open pits, unimproved pit latrines, unlined pits, no slabs, prone to flooding etc \* This is indicative of the reach and scale of the initiative in reaching new users with its products and services in terms of the service level that is being provided (as defined by JMP).
